text: Preview: NVKE is available as a preview. APIs, configuration and behavior can change between releases, and we do not recommend NVKE for production workloads. See Preview status and known limitations . Run a managed Kubernetes service on your own NVIDIA GPU infrastructure. NVIDIA Kubernetes® Engine (NVKE) provides the management plane that platform teams install to create and operate Kubernetes clusters for their customers. Each workload cluster has its own Kubernetes control plane, etcd and node pools. You operate the NVKE management plane; your customers use their clusters through the Kubernetes API and kubectl . Preview: NVKE is available as a preview. APIs, configuration and behavior can change between releases, and we do not recommend NVKE for production workloads. See Preview status and known limitations . Get started · Documentation · Contribute · Get help The local quickstart runs on a Linux host or VM, amd64 or arm64 , with at least 6 CPUs, 12 GiB of free memory and 100 GiB of free disk . It requires Docker, virtual TPM support and the tools listed in the guide. Follow its setup through workload-cluster creation and confirm the cluster's nodes report Ready . On macOS, use the local site guide , which runs the evaluation inside a Colima virtual machine. For a real installation, you supply the machines, networking, node images and registries, and configure access to NVIDIA Infra Controller (NICo) . NICo is the sole compatible infrastructure provider at preview. The platform and version reference lists validated combinations and pinned dependencies. The preview needs explicit operator configuration: API authentication is off and the API uses plain HTTP after installation. Configure API authentication and protected access before admitting callers. The management cluster does not upgrade, scale or replace itself, and there is no management-plane upgrade or backup/restore procedure. FDE node images are for evaluation and provide no data-at-rest confidentiality. Read the known limitations before choosing an evaluation or installation path. The diagram shows the NVKE product family, how it sits on NICo and your GPU machines, and which components talk to each other. NVKE is not a Kubernetes distribution and not a Cluster API flavour. It is a self-hosting factory for Kubernetes clusters : a throwaway seed cluster stands up a management cluster, and the management plane on it then provisions and lifecycle-manages many isolated workload clusters on demand. An installation has two kinds of Kubernetes cluster: Read What is NVKE for the operator workflow and Architecture for the implementation and data flows. Use Go 1.27.3 , the version pinned in go.work , and GNU Make 4 or later . Public Go modules must be reachable on the first build. Flox is optional and supplies the repository's development tools; on macOS, it also supplies GNU Make 4. See Development for toolchain setup. git clone https://github.com/dsx-ai-factory/nvke.git cd nvke make build This builds the workspace and writes nine binaries to bin/ : agent , updater , controller , nvkectl , capd-reboot-controller , nvke-os-image-check , management-engine , tenant-api and operator-api . Building does not start a management plane or create a cluster. The node agent runs on Linux. The workspace guide explains the modules and outputs. For local services and test environments, see Local development setup . Before submitting a change, follow CONTRIBUTING.md and run make preflight ; it selects checks for the modules you changed. The documentation index links the remaining guides and references. Contributions, bug reports and documentation improvements are welcome. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md ; open an issue before substantial work so maintainers can agree on the approach.
